scenes.narration: Templates. Client Libraries — Fundamentals (Part 1 of 2). In this video we review 5 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What are clientlibs in AEM?
scenes.heading: The built-in solution in AEM for delivering CSS and JavaScript
scenes.body: Clientlibs are the built-in solution in AEM for delivering CSS and JavaScript, streamlining the organization, management, and delivery of front-end code within an AEM project.

scenes.question: What are the advantages of using clientlibs?
scenes.heading: Centralized management, improved performance via aggregation, reusability, scalability, security, auditing, and versioning
scenes.body: Clientlibs offer centralized management (single repository location), improved performance (aggregated into single files, reducing requests), reusability across pages/components, scalability, security via access controls, auditing, and versioning.

scenes.question: What is a client-side library folder, structurally?
scenes.heading: A repository node of type cq:ClientLibraryFolder, typically stored under /apps
scenes.body: A client-side library folder is a repository node of type cq:ClientLibraryFolder. It is a collection of JavaScript, CSS, and other resources reusable across multiple pages or components, typically stored under /apps.

scenes.question: What are the two important properties of a client-side library folder?
scenes.heading: categories (identifies which category or categories the library belongs to) and allowProxy (allows proxy servlet access)
scenes.body: The important properties of a client-side library folder are categories, a multi-valued property identifying the categories the JS/CSS files fall into, and allowProxy, which allows access to the library via the proxy servlet.

scenes.question: What does a client-side library folder typically contain?
scenes.heading: Source JS/CSS files, static resources like icons/fonts, and a js.txt and/or css.txt file listing which files to merge
scenes.body: A client-side library folder contains the JS and/or CSS source files, static resources that support styles (icons, web fonts, etc.), and one js.txt and/or one css.txt file identifying the source files to merge into the generated output.
